title: soundfiler
description: read and write tables to soundfiles

messages.description: number of samples (when reading a file)
sample rate, header size, channels, bytes per sample, endianness

methods.description: reads a file into one or more arrays, one per channel; optional flags: -wave, -aiff, -caf, -next, -skip <float>, -resize, -maxsize <float>, -ascii, -raw <list>
writes one or more arrays to a file, one per channel; optional flags: -wave, -aiff, -caf, -next, -ascii, -big, -little, -skip <float>, -nframes <float>, -bytes <float>, -normalize, -rate <float>

body:
The soundfiler object reads and writes floating point arrays to binary soundfiles which may contain uncompressed 2- or 3-byte integer ("pcm") or 4-byte floating point samples in wave, aiff, caf, next, or ascii text formats. The number of channels of the soundfile need not match the number of arrays given (extras are dropped and unsupplied channels are zeroed out).

The number of channels is limited to 64.

Flags for 'read' messages:
- -wave, -aiff, -caf, -next
- -skip <sample frames to skip in file>
- -resize (resizes arrays to the size of the sound file)
- -maxsize <maximum number of samples we can resize to>
- -raw <headersize> <channels> <bytespersample> <endianness>: ignores all header and type information, instead of letting soundfiler figure out which of the known soundfile formats the file belongs to. Endianness is "l" ("little") for Intel machines or "b" ("big") for older PPC Macintoshes. You can give "n" (natural) to take the byte order your machine prefers.
- -ascii: reads a file containing ascii numbers. May be combined with -resize. Newlines in the file are ignored, and non-numeric fields are replaced by zero. If multiple arrays are specified, the first elements of each array should come first in the file, followed by all the second elements and so on (interleaved).

Flags for 'write' messages:
- -wave, -aiff, -caf, -next, -ascii
- -big, -little (sample endianness)
- -skip <number of sample frames to skip in array>
- -nframes <maximum number to write>
- -bytes <2, 3, or 4>
- -normalize
- -rate <sample rate>
